title: Orientation-dependent plastic deformation mechanisms and competition with stress-induced phase transformation in microscale NiTi
notes: No introduction or methods in the packet, so HYP/DES/PRC carry source=text with requires_unseen. Two spine branches leave the compression act: the [001] branch (localized band -> deformation twinned austenite) and the [112] branch (whole-pillar single-slip traces -> no superelasticity, 12% permanent strain); they reconverge on the common martensite structure (B19' + B2, (001) compound twins in a herringbone), which identifies the herringbone MT, which with the Schmid-factor maps gives the orientation-dependent competition. F7 and F8 are contour maps of a computed response over the standard stereographic triangle; modality xy_curve was used (modality_notes: 'contour of a response'), not orientation_distribution, whose corpus use is measured texture pole figures. F4 is tier C with no panel crops, so its nodes carry figs=['F4'] and panel_ids=[]. Three audits: a1 (SADPs lack the mirrored (001)B19' spot set), a2 (text_silent: the [001] corner survives as a low outlier in the herringbone CRSS map), a3 (MD omits dislocation plasticity). Judge review: n9 was split, the ~7.3% residual strain becoming the side claim n27, which the dislocation-stabilisation MEC n12 (now off spine) explains and which qualifies n9.

nodes.label: [001]-oriented pillars are superelastic: a stress-induced transformation plateau from ~430 MPa and hysteresis loops that close on unloading
After the large strain burst the [001] pillar keeps ~7.3% residual strain, more than the ~6.3% burst, so part of the stress-induced martensite does not revert

nodes.label: Plastic deformation of the [001] pillar is localized to one narrow band; the rest of the pillar shaft stays featureless
Austenite inside the [001] band is deformation twinned: the austenite lattices on the two sides of the band are rotated by 29 deg
Dislocations lie on (-110) planes parallel to the compression axis in the austenite next to the martensite plates of the [001] pillar
Dislocations left at the austenite/martensite interfaces stabilise part of the martensite, so it does not revert on unloading and the residual strain exceeds the strain burst
[112]-oriented pillars are not superelastic: unloading is linear and ~12% of the strain is permanent
Deformation of the [112] pillar is spread over the whole pillar as many parallel traces of a single slip plane
The austenite islands of the [112] pillar carry dislocation contrast on one (-110) plane only, with no deformation twinning of the austenite

attrs.image_note: the absence of austenite deformation twins rests on this single field of view

nodes.label: Both deformed pillars keep B19' martensite coexisting with B2 austenite: domains inside the [001] band, islands in the [112] pillar
The martensite domains are built of (001)B19' compound twins a few nanometres wide, arranged in a herringbone structure

attrs.image_note: F6 shows the deformed [112] pillar and the MD cell only; the matching [001] microstructure is said to be in Fig. S2 of the Supplementary Material

nodes.label: The operative transformation is the herringbone B2-B19' MT that produces (001)B19' compound twins, not the conventional B2-B19' MT with [011]B19' type II twins
The stress to induce martensite is lowest near [001] and higher at [112]: the [001] pillar transforms from ~430 MPa while the [112] pillar reaches ~595 MPa with no transformation plateau

Orientation sets the competition: at [001] slip has zero Schmid factor while herringbone MT (0.520) and {112}<111> twinning (0.471) are near maximal, whereas at [112] {011}<100> slip is near maximal (0.471) and herringbone MT only 0.348
Converted to CRSS, the MD transformation stresses stay far more nearly orientation independent under the herringbone Schmid factors than under the conventional ones

attrs.verdict: herringbone MT is the better description

nodes.label: Orientation decides whether microscale NiTi deforms by herringbone stress-induced MT with superelastic recovery ([001]) or by {011}<100> slip with permanent strain ([112])
Compression axes near [001] should be chosen where recoverable superelastic strain is wanted; axes near [112] favour slip and permanent deformation
The MD simulations omit dislocation plasticity and did not reproduce deformation twinning, so they support only the transformation branch of the argument

requires_unseen: the stated MD limitations come from the F8 linked text

nodes.label: Conventional theory of martensite: B2-B19' with [011]B19' type II twins as lattice-invariant shear cannot produce (001)B19' compound twins
Schmid law: resolved shear stress equals applied stress times the Schmid factor, so the CRSS of one mechanism must be orientation independent
(001)B19' compound twins a few nanometres wide have been reported before in NiTi shape memory alloys
Dislocations left at austenite/martensite interfaces are known to stabilise martensite against reversion
XRD peaks index to B2 austenite (100),(110),(200),(210),(211),(220) with weak Ti4Ni2O (511),(440),(822)/(660),(10 2 2) reflections
